clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: your four weeks building with Silas at Alder Creek in July 2008, where you were too drained for conversation with your mother and she pressed to visit you, kept the door shut on her when she came, and you stopped speaking to her when you left for nursing school in Marlow Sound in August 2008. clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within the next two and a half years: your contact with your mother eased off slightly once she came along, your job steadied and your anxiety dropped in June 2019, though by October 2019 you felt you ought to be driving your projects forward and your anxiety rose again as you started a sleeping pill; Wren's cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, her mother Imogen's memory began slipping by 2015 and she lashed out when muddled by October 2018, and Leo and his family returned to live nearby by August 2019. In late October 2019, around her mother Frances's retirement party at the lake house, Wren was swamped with one thing after another and you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her; her family talks all day and nothing happens to one that the others don't hear—tight fusion among them. Wren settled once the weekend had a plan and the dinner went well, but you awoke from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose; your anxiety rose and you felt you did not belong, and Wren grew anxious when you had had no sleep at family occasions. The shifts moved between you and Wren and between you both and her family across the months; your anxiety rising and falling alongside hers, your distance from her family when together, your pull toward your own mother steadying with shorter regular calls to soften the distance that piled up.
